children: The benchmark indices declined around 1.75 percent on November 23 amid sharp profit booking and weak market breadth. On the NSE, 2,288 stocks ended lower, compared with 1,019 stocks that advanced. After a day of sharp selling, the market could witness a rebound. Here are some short-term trading ideas to watch:
Jay Thakkar, Vice President & Head of Derivatives and Quant Research at ICICI Securities

Coforge has provided a muti-year breakout and with that there has been long additions in this stock in the futures segment as well which is also positive for it in the near term. As per the options data, Rs 2,140 has the highest Call base and since it has managed to just close above the same the probability of Call unwinding is higher. The maximum pain for the December series is at Rs 2,100 and the stock is trading well above the same. Buy Coforge Futures in the range of Rs 2,120-2,150, with a stop-loss below Rs 2,070.
Torrent Pharmaceuticals has relatively underperformed its peers in the last uptrend, however, recently there has been long additions in the near term indicating a potential short-term uptrend.

As per the options data, Rs 4,800 strike has the highest Call base whereas Rs 4,700 has the highest Put base, hence the stop-loss is recommended below Rs 4,690 whereas above Rs 4,800, one can expect further upward momentum due to Call unwinding. The maximum pain is at Rs 4,700 level and the stock is trading well above the same indicating strength in the near term. Buy Torrent Pharma Futures in the range of Rs 4,780-4,800, with a stop-loss below Rs 4,690.

Bajaj Auto after having rallied significantly due to short covering is now facing hurdle at the higher levels and recently it has been underperforming its peers and there has been fresh shorts that are now getting added at the current levels which is a negative sign.

As per the options data, Rs 10,800 and Rs 11,000 strikes have the highest Call base which will act as a hurdle whereas Rs 10,500 and Rs 10,000 strikes have the highest Put base which will act as a support. The stock is trading below its maximum pain level of Rs 10,800 which is also negative in the near term. Sell Bajaj Auto Futures in the range of Rs 10,600-10,700 with stop-loss above Rs 11,300.
Jigar Patel, Senior Manager - Equity Research at Anand Rathi

Siemens Energy has closed above its 20 DEMA following a brief pullback, indicating a potential improvement in its short-term price structure. Having said that, the daily RSI is hovering around the 50 mark, suggesting a gradual recovery in momentum.

Meanwhile, the hourly RSI continues to maintain its bullish range of 80–40, indicating that buying momentum remains supportive. Sustaining above the 20 DEMA, along with continued strength in hourly RSI, could support further upside in the coming sessions. Traders may consider entering long positions in the Rs 2,980 – 2,940 zone, with target of Rs 4,150.

Brigade Enterprises has started forming a sequence of higher highs and higher lows, indicating an improvement in its overall price structure. Additionally, the stock is sustaining above its 10 and 20 DEMA, which were earlier acting as resistance but have now turned into support. This shift in the role of moving averages suggests improving buying interest and a strengthening short-term trend. Traders may consider entering long positions in the zone Rs 583-573 with target of Rs 620.

Emami has developed a three-point bullish divergence on the weekly chart, indicating improving underlying momentum and the possibility of a sustained recovery. Additionally, the price is trading above its 10 and 20 DEMA, reflecting a positive price structure.

On the hourly chart, RSI continues to maintain its bullish range of 80–40, suggesting that buying momentum remains intact. The combination of positive weekly momentum and supportive short-term indicators strengthens the overall bullish outlook. Traders may consider entering long positions in the Rs 420-410 zone, with target of Rs 475.
Vidnyan Sawant, Head of Research at GEPL Capital
Union Bank of India | CMP: Rs 208.2

Union Bank of India has been maintaining a strong primary uptrend on the weekly chart since October 2021, characterized by a consistent higher high–higher low formation. Recently, the stock has registered a significant breakout from a long-term Inverse Head & Shoulders pattern, formed since August 2015, and moved into fresh multi-year high territory. The breakout is supported by a notable surge in trading volumes, indicating strong buying participation.

The stock is comfortably trading above its 50, 100 and 200-week EMAs, with positive alignment reinforcing the bullish trend. Momentum indicators also remain supportive, with MACD generating a fresh bullish crossover above the zero line and RSI placed at 64, reflecting strong positive momentum.
Traders may maintain a positive positional bias with a stop-loss of Rs 190 on a weekly closing basis, while the stock has the potential to move towards Rs 242 in the coming weeks.
Motilal Oswal Financial Services | CMP: Rs 1,235

Motilal Oswal witnessed a breakout from a prolonged consolidation pattern on the weekly chart a few weeks ago, which had been developing since October 2024. The stock has shown strong follow-through buying post-breakout and is consistently trading near its fresh all-time highs, indicating a strong bullish undertone.

On the daily chart, the stock is comfortably sustaining above its key 50, 100 and 200-day EMAs, with positive alignment reinforcing the prevailing uptrend and sustained buying interest. Furthermore, the weekly RSI is placed at 68 and trending upward, indicating strengthening bullish momentum.
Somil Mehta, Head of Retail Research at Mirae Asset ShareKhan

Dixon Technologies is forming higher highs and higher lows on the daily chart and is trading above the key daily moving averages. After a few sessions of sideways movement in the form of a flag, it broke out of the pattern on Monday and got its uptrend going again.
From here, the stock can head towards Rs 14,000 – 14,400 in the coming sessions. If it dips, the 12,900 – 13,050 zone should act as support.

Narayana Hrudayalaya has been forming an inverse head and shoulders pattern. On Monday, it broke out and closed above the neckline. Volumes have also picked up over the last couple of sessions, which suggests buyers are returning. That can help momentum build in the coming sessions, with the stock moving towards Rs 2,090 – 2,150. On the downside, the Rs 1,910 – 1,920 zone is a key support area.
Allied Blenders and Distillers | CMP: Rs 802.85

Allied Blenders and Distillers broke out of a cup and handle pattern on November 17, and has since been holding above the breakout point. On the lower timeframe, it has bounced from the key moving averages and cleared a minor consolidation.
The daily momentum indicator is bullish, and the hourly indicator turned bullish with a crossover on Monday. Together, these point to stronger upside momentum in the coming sessions.
As long as the Rs 779 low holds, the stock can climb to the Rs 840 – 855 zone. A fall below Rs 779 would put this view at risk, as that is the crucial support.

title: Trade Spotlight: How should you trade Coforge, Torrent Pharma, Siemens Energy, Union Bank of India, Motilal Oswal, and others on November 25?
